title: Help & support
description: Set up your daybook, connect your calendar, review receipts and get help with Cuekeeper.
introduction: Find an answer below, or get in touch if something isn’t working as expected.

sections.title: Start your daybook
paragraphs: An event is useful before its client, schedule or fee is complete. Add details as they’re confirmed.
steps: Choose Add Event and enter the name and dates. An event has at most one client; leave it blank if it isn’t known yet.
Add the client, role, work arrangement and location. The timezone follows the location (see Timezones).
Add sessions with their start, end and call times. An incomplete schedule is fine.
Record the fee when you know it. Once the work is done, Payments shows whether the event is ready to invoice.
after: In Upcoming, Now shows your next call and the next 72 hours of work; Plan lists booking, schedule and fee gaps to settle and what’s coming up.
Booking, session confirmation, coverage, invoicing and payment are tracked separately. Booking an event doesn’t confirm its sessions or mark it paid.

You can enter work offline and without connecting Calendar; iCloud sync, maps, weather and cloud backups need a connection. Cuekeeper requires iOS or iPadOS 27, and automatic receipt extraction needs Apple Intelligence on a compatible device.

sections.title: Records haven’t arrived on another device
paragraphs: A finished transfer on one device doesn’t mean another device has received every change.
steps: Make sure both devices use the intended Apple Account with iCloud available, are online and have Cuekeeper open.
On each device, check the Your data panel in Settings. For an account problem, fix it in your device settings, then choose Check Again.
If the issue persists, contact support with the exact error and which device holds the missing changes.
sections.note: Don’t delete or reinstall Cuekeeper to troubleshoot unsynced work, and keep the device with the original records intact. Sync is not a backup.

sections.title: Connect or troubleshoot Calendar
paragraphs: One device publishes event placeholders and confirmed, covering sessions to a calendar you choose.
steps: On that device, open Settings → Integrations → Calendar, allow full Calendar access and choose a writable calendar.
To publish updates, open Cuekeeper on that device while online so changes from your other devices can arrive.
If a session is missing, check that it’s confirmed, covering and has complete times.
after: To move publishing, disconnect Calendar on the old device before connecting the new one. If the old device is unavailable, contact support rather than deleting calendar data.

Cuekeeper only updates its own entries; don’t remove unrelated events to troubleshoot. New entries have no alerts, and alerts you add are kept. Your calendar provider’s sharing settings apply to published entries.

sections.title: Keep event and local times straight
paragraphs: An event’s timezone comes from its track, otherwise its typed location, otherwise your Home location in Settings → User settings. For remote or hybrid work, set Your location to also see your local time.

Changing the location can change the timezone. Sessions keep their local clock times, so the moments they refer to move. Copied sessions keep their clock times in the destination event’s timezone, and times skipped by daylight saving are rejected.
If a time looks wrong, check the event’s location and work arrangement first, and review dates near midnight or daylight-saving changes.

sections.title: Back up and recover your work
paragraphs: Backups are manual copies of your daybook, saved to your private iCloud storage or exported as a ZIP to Files. They include events, sessions, clients, financial history, expenses and receipt photos on this device, but not Calendar connections or device preferences. Keep the ZIP intact; you don’t need to unzip it to restore.
steps: Open Settings → Recovery & backups → Backups. On iPhone, the Files actions are in the toolbar menu.
Choose Back Up Now for iCloud, or Export to Files for a ZIP. Changes still arriving through sync may not be included.
To restore, choose Restore beside an iCloud copy, or Import a Backup and select the ZIP (also offered at first launch). If Files can’t open it, download it there first.
Once Cuekeeper has checked the backup, confirm Restore Backup. Restore adds missing and deleted records without overwriting newer edits or payments.
For a single deleted event or session, use Recently Deleted. Restore the parent event first if needed.
after: Keep Cuekeeper open until the operation finishes. You can cancel while preparing or reading, but not while a restore is saving or an iCloud backup is committing.

Each archive is limited to 512 MB, including up to 32 MB of record details and 200,000 records, and you can keep 50 iCloud copies. Restoring also needs free device storage. If you reach a limit, contact support rather than deleting financial history.
Damaged, incomplete or unsupported backups are rejected before anything is restored. Keep another good copy, and don’t edit files inside the ZIP.

Recently Deleted normally keeps items for 30 days. Restored records sync to your other devices and can reappear in a connected calendar. Deleting a backup doesn’t affect your daybook; delete exported copies wherever you saved them.
sections.note: Exported ZIP files aren’t encrypted and contain personal and financial records and receipt images. Store them somewhere you trust and never send a whole backup to support.

sections.title: Scan, review and save a receipt
paragraphs: Event expenses don’t change the fee, but a draft receipt holds up its event’s invoice until finished. Finished receipts marked Reimbursable can be rebilled on an invoice. Business costs, such as software or insurance, have no event, need no photo and are never rebilled.
steps: Choose Scan Receipt in Expenses, the Upcoming header or an event, then confirm the event. Scan one page per expense, or cancel the camera to import a photo. If camera access is off, choose Open Settings.
Check the suggested merchant, date, total, currency, included tax and category against the receipt.
Save, or choose Keep Draft to finish later. Reopen an expense to edit it or replace an unreadable photo.
For a business cost, choose Business under What it’s for. Repeats monthly offers next month’s cost under To finish when it’s due; it isn’t added automatically.
after: Extraction uses Vision and Apple’s on-device Foundation Models, so Apple Intelligence must be on with its model ready. If a receipt is too long for the on-device model, its recognized text (not the photo) is sent to Apple Private Cloud Compute, which needs a connection; Cuekeeper tells you when this happens. If extraction is unavailable, enter the fields manually.
Photos are saved as drafts before extraction, but an interruption can lose form edits made since the last save.

Expenses support positive totals in USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, NZD and CHF. Cuekeeper doesn’t split receipts, convert currencies or calculate tax. For the Action Button, assign the Scan Receipt shortcut.

sections.title: Capture Wallet expense drafts
paragraphs: A Shortcuts personal automation can pass transaction fields to Cuekeeper when you tap a Wallet card. It isn’t a feed of every charge, and Cuekeeper never reads your Wallet or banking history.
steps: In Shortcuts → Automation → +, choose Transaction (or Wallet) and select your cards under When I tap. Labels and fields vary by system version.
Choose Run Immediately, then Next. Create a blank automation and add Cuekeeper → Capture Expense.

Map Merchant, Amount (a number), Currency (a code such as USD) and Transaction date where available, and leave missing fields blank. Map Transaction ID only if a stable one is supplied; never substitute a merchant or amount.
Save the automation. Drafts appear under To finish in Expenses and in Payments. Attach the receipt, choose an active event and review the fields before saving.
after: Your phone may need to be unlocked. Without stable IDs, matching merchants, dates and amounts aren’t treated as duplicates, and drafts captured offline on separate devices aren’t merged. Remove personal or duplicate drafts from the draft list.
Receipt extraction fills missing fields and shows differences from the captured payment.

Optional completion reminders are in Settings → Integrations → Wallet Automation. If notifications are off or silenced by Focus, the draft is still in the app. Use Scan Receipt, not Capture Expense, for the Action Button.

sections.title: Keep widgets up to date
paragraphs: Add a widget from the Home or Lock Screen widget picker. Widgets show today’s remaining sessions, later days and the next call from the last snapshot the app wrote. They don’t sync iCloud themselves, and the system decides when they refresh.
If a widget looks out of date, open Cuekeeper, let your latest changes arrive, then check again. Use your system privacy settings to keep event or client names off the Lock Screen.

sections.title: Understand invoices and payments
paragraphs: An unknown fee isn’t a fee of zero. A quantity/rate breakdown replaces the overall fee only when you choose Use Breakdown Total.

Payments shows a month at a time. An event is ready to invoice once it clears four steps: Fee, Client, Work and Receipts. A held-up event names its gap and offers an action for each step. The client needs Bill to, Email, Address and Terms, and no receipt can still be a draft.

Choose Invoice on a ready client group or in the toolbar, pick what to bill, then record how it went out. Work that isn’t ready can still be included. Marking an invoice sent sets its due date from the client’s terms. Switch to Invoices to see every invoice and payment, record a payment, mark an invoice sent or void it.

An invoice covers one client and currency and can include finished reimbursable receipts, each on one active invoice. Line amounts are snapshots, so later fee edits don’t change them. Partial payments reduce the invoice balance rather than a particular event’s.
Balances stay separate by currency. Cuekeeper doesn’t create or send invoice documents, connect to banking, calculate tax or convert currencies.
If sync shows conflicting financial changes, resolve them explicitly. Don’t record a payment twice because another device hasn’t received it yet.

sections.title: Privacy and removing data
paragraphs: Your daybook is stored on your device and syncs through your private iCloud database. Receipt extraction runs on-device, except that the text of a receipt too long for the on-device model goes to Apple Private Cloud Compute. Receipt photos sync and are included in backups.

Removing an item from Recently Deleted ends recovery but isn’t secure erasure. Deleting the app doesn’t delete iCloud records or backups, and there’s no in-app command to erase everything. The developer can’t access or erase your iCloud daybook, so contact support before removing data you may need.

sections.title: Still need a hand?
paragraphs: Email cuekeeper@arjunakankipati.com with your Cuekeeper version and build (Settings → About), device model, iOS/iPadOS version, what you expected and the steps that led to the problem.

Redact personal details from screenshots. Never send your Apple Account password, a verification code or a whole backup, and include receipts or financial details only if they’re needed to explain the issue.
